subject.title: CLI-backed helper paths still bypass CLI dispatch on latest main

question: Where should OpenClaw resolve CLI execution providers for the remaining helper and registration paths so diagnostics, slug generation, prewarm, and subagent/gateway admission match runtime dispatch without storing CLI runtime ids as canonical model providers?
rationale: The code evidence shows real divergence, but the permanent boundary affects local CLI credentials, embedded/API billing behavior, auth diagnostics, and session metadata semantics, so automation should not choose that architecture alone.

options.title: Resolve At Execution Boundaries
options.body: Add a shared execution-provider handoff near helper dispatch and run registration while keeping persisted model/provider state canonical.

options.title: Document Intentional Embedded Diagnostics
options.body: If probes or slug generation should remain embedded-only, document and test that contract so it is not treated as a CLI dispatch bug.

options.title: Land Narrow Slices First
options.body: Keep this broad tracker open while maintainers review the narrower probe, memory/preflight, and subagent items before choosing a cross-surface repair.

recommendation.title: Resolve At Execution Boundaries
recommendation.body: Add a shared execution-provider handoff near helper dispatch and run registration while keeping persisted model/provider state canonical.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete is the strongest routing owner from recent gateway/session/model-status history and can decide the cross-surface auth/session boundary.
